preconditions.expression: all(c in {'#', '.'} for c in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each line of input (after the first) contains only '#' or '.' characters.
Input contains at least one test case (T >= 1).
First line is a valid integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 1,000,000).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= len(P) <= 1000000 for P in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each passageway string P has length between 1 and 1,000,000.

preconditions.expression: all(P[0] == '#' and P[-1] == '#' for P in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: First and last characters of each P are '#'.

postconditions.description: Output contains exactly T lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(out.isdigit() and 0 <= int(out) <= len(P) for out, P in zip(stdout.splitlines(), stdin.splitlines()[1:]))
postconditions.description: Each output line is a non-negative integer ≤ length of the corresponding P.

postconditions.expression: all(int(out) == days_to_cross(P) for out, P in zip(stdout.splitlines(), stdin.splitlines()[1:]))
postconditions.description: For each P, the output is the number of days required to cross the passageway, where days_to_cross(P) is defined as follows: Start with max_jump = 1. Traverse P from left to right, tracking the current position and max_jump. For each '.' encountered, if the distance to the next '#' exceeds max_jump, increment days by 1 and set max_jump to that distance. The total days is the sum of all such increments.
